feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — Syntax is abstract and symbolic, not a tangible object.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — All programming languages are human-designed artifacts.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not derived from biological structures.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — The syntax itself does not consume or depend on power.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — No inherent physical or structural characteristics.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Only visible when instantiated in code or diagrams.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Exists as an abstract rule system.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Syntax defines rules but does not act independently.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Excluded — While designed, it is not a functioning unit but a representational system.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Syntax guides behavior in code but does not emit effects alone.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — It encodes logic but does not process it independently.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Does not transform itself or any system on its own.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Not interactive apart from use in programming environments.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Implemented in systems, but syntax itself is abstract.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Cannot perform actions or adapt autonomously.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Many systems can exist independent of any one syntax.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Syntax is a formal symbolic notation system.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Conveys meaning and instruction to both humans and compilers.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Strictly constrained by formal grammars and parsing logic.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Built from tokens, operators, and hierarchically structured rules.
feedback.Normative: Included — Prescribes how valid programs must be written.
feedback.Meta: Included — Can be used to describe and generate other language rules (e.g., via grammars).
feedback.Temporal: Excluded — Syntax is static; execution order is defined by semantics, not syntax itself.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Exists as a set of rules used in digital computation.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Only meaningful through shared conventions among developers and institutions.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Standardized by language committees, universities, and organizations.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not inherently tied to identity or social roles.
feedback.Regulated: Excluded — Defined and standardized, but not enforced by external governance or law.
feedback.Economically Significant: Excluded — Syntax itself is not traded or valued in economic exchange.
feedback.Politicised: Excluded — The syntax rules themselves are not involved in political power or ideology.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — Syntax is standard, not ceremonial or culturally symbolic.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Excluded — The syntax carries no intrinsic moral content or consequences.

encoding_notes: This encoding isolates programming language syntax as a formal symbolic structure with no functional agency or physical embodiment. It is purely abstract and institutional — governed by rules, not by regulation, politics, or ethics. Traits like Temporal, Economic, and Politicised are excluded to preserve a rigorously minimal semantic fingerprint.
